records: {primary_actor} and {secondary_actor} are in an openly dangerous standoff over {target}, but violence has not yet become inevitable.
Everyone can see that escalation is possible and that words, movement or withdrawal still matter.
What does each side need to avoid backing down empty-handed?
Which action would be interpreted as escalation even if unintended?
Fear, pride, reinforcements, witnesses or narrowing space increase instability.
Someone lowers a weapon, makes a demand, receives new information or loses control of the situation.
handoff into an owning Encounter if violence begins
{secondary_actor} intentionally blocks {route} toward {target}, creating a confrontation before any specific resolution method is chosen.
The blocker has a reason, leverage or fear that can potentially be understood or bypassed.
Can the goal be reached without forcing this exact crossing?
Time, crowding, allies or approaching danger make prolonged deadlock costly.
The blocker's motive becomes clearer, another route appears or a third party intervenes.
transition to an owning Encounter if force begins
{primary_actor} directly accuses {secondary_actor} over {past_event} while consequences depend on how the confrontation develops.
The accusation is public or private as the consumer chooses; guilt is not established by the template.
What evidence actually supports the accusation?
What response would change the accuser's confidence?
Audience, status, anger or time pressure may turn inquiry into conflict.
New evidence, admission, counteraccusation or uncertainty changes the frame.
{community} is close to collective confrontation over {target}, with several voices pulling toward escalation or restraint.
No single actor fully controls the crowd and the mood can still move in more than one direction.
Which grievance is shared versus merely adjacent?
Who has credibility with different parts of the crowd?
Rumor, visible force, injury, delay or symbolic acts can swing group behavior quickly.
A speaker emerges, evidence arrives, authorities change posture or a triggering incident occurs.
handoff to owning Encounter if violence erupts
{secondary_actor} demands action involving {target} and holds meaningful leverage over {primary_actor} or {resource}.
The leverage is real but does not automatically make compliance the only rational response.
What exactly can the demander actually do?
What alternatives reduce or change the leverage?
A deadline, vulnerable resource or public commitment makes delay expensive.
Leverage weakens, strengthens, is challenged or becomes shared by another party.
{primary_actor} and {secondary_actor} independently pursue {target} and meet before either has secured it.
Competition is obvious, but cooperation, racing, bargaining and disengagement remain possible.
Is the objective divisible or shareable?
What does each rival know or control that the other lacks?
A closing window or environmental change raises the cost of prolonged confrontation.
The target changes state, a new threat appears or one rival offers terms.
{primary_actor} and {secondary_actor} disagree about control, access or responsibility at {location}.
The boundary may be legal, customary, practical or symbolic; the template does not decide who is right.
Which rule or custom does each side invoke?
Is the disagreement about the line itself or what the line permits?
Ongoing use, witnesses or resource pressure makes delay create precedent.
A record, respected mediator, physical change or new use case complicates the boundary.
dispute remains active without immediate escalation
{primary_actor} arrives while {secondary_actor} and {outsider} are already in conflict over {target}.
The situation can be influenced, but intervening may create obligations or misunderstandings.
What is actually happening versus what it looks like at first glance?
What kind of intervention is justified with current information?
The conflict may escalate faster than facts can be established.
One party asks for help, new context appears or immediate harm becomes more likely.
handoff to owning Encounter if force begins
{primary_actor} openly challenges a decision or legitimacy claim made by {authority_actor} concerning {target}.
The challenge has enough support or visibility that it cannot be dismissed without consequence.
Is the challenge about procedure, outcome or legitimacy?
Who is watching and what standard do they care about?
Public commitment makes compromise harder while delay can look like weakness.
A concession, procedural option, supporter or embarrassing fact changes the balance.
challenge continues into a larger political track
{secondary_actor} communicates that continued action toward {target} will trigger a serious response.
The warning is credible enough to matter but may still be bluff, boundary, deterrence or invitation to negotiate.
What response is actually being threatened?
What would make the warning negotiable, irrelevant or more credible?
Continuing, pausing or testing the warning each carries different costs.
The warning is clarified, contradicted, reinforced or overtaken by events.
proceed and hand off consequences to owning domains
During {event}, {primary_actor} faces simultaneous needs involving {target}, {resource} and {relationship} that cannot all receive full attention.
Each need is meaningful and none is declared objectively correct by the template.
Which need is time-critical versus merely important?
Can attention be delegated, sequenced or partially shared?
The same limited window closes across several priorities at once.
One problem resolves itself, worsens or becomes connected to another.
{secondary_actor} can solve an immediate problem involving {target}, but {relationship} makes accepting help complicated.
The offered help is plausibly effective and plausibly costly in nontechnical ways.
Who controls the terms of the help?
What new obligation, access or trust signal would acceptance create?
The immediate problem worsens while alternatives take time.
The helper changes terms, demonstrates sincerity or reveals another motive.
New {evidence} materially affects a plan already underway toward {target}.
The existing plan remains possible, but its assumptions or desirability are no longer stable.
Which part of the plan does the new information actually invalidate?
Momentum, sunk cost or timing makes replanning expensive.
The evidence is confirmed, challenged or accompanied by a new opportunity.
{primary_actor} attends {event} where a private interest involving {target} competes with visible social expectations.
The public activity continues independently of whether the private objective is pursued.
How much attention can be diverted without appearing strange?
What public participation creates useful access or information?
Social obligations and event timing limit private action windows.
A key person arrives, the schedule changes or the private objective becomes unexpectedly public.
Progress on {target} unexpectedly creates {obstacle} affecting {community} or {resource}.
The original success remains real; the new cost must be addressed without pretending success was failure.
Who bears the new cost and who benefited from the success?
Momentum favors continuing while consequences accumulate elsewhere.
The side effect expands, becomes manageable or reveals a second benefit/cost.
The Local Rule Changes the Easy Plan
An ordinary plan involving {target} becomes complicated by a local rule, custom or authority tied to {location}.
The rule is meaningful enough to respect but may allow negotiation, exception or alternative approaches.
What purpose does the rule serve locally?
What alternatives preserve the goal without simply ignoring the rule?
Time, reputation or access costs increase if the issue is mishandled.
A local sponsor, exception, dispute or deeper reason for the rule changes options.
While responding to {pressure}, an unexpected {opportunity} connected to {target} appears.
Taking advantage of it is optional and may compete with stabilization or safety.
What makes the opportunity genuinely time-limited?
Can it be captured without neglecting the crisis?
Attention and resources are already committed elsewhere.
The opportunity becomes safer, riskier, more valuable or less unique.
Someone Knows More Than They Can Say
{secondary_actor} appears to know important information about {target} but is constrained by {obstacle} from sharing it directly.
The constraint may be loyalty, law, fear, uncertainty or another consumer-supplied reason.
What can the actor safely communicate indirectly?
Is the constraint real, self-imposed or misunderstood?
Pressure for answers can damage trust or increase the actor's risk.
A safer channel, changed circumstance, third party or new evidence loosens or tightens the constraint.
Progress toward {target} unexpectedly depends on cooperation from {outsider} whose interests are only partly known.
The outsider has real leverage but is not automatically enemy, ally or neutral tool.
What does the outsider want now?
How much trust is actually required for cooperation?
Time pressure makes relationship-building and verification costly.
The outsider makes a request, reveals competence, withholds something or gains another option.
A scene that began around {target} is overtaken by {event} or {unknown_factor}, making the original purpose only one concern among several.
The shift is substantial but does not erase prior choices or force one new objective.
Which original goals still matter after the shift?
What new concern deserves immediate attention versus later follow-up?
Old commitments and new urgency compete for the same limited attention.
The new event stabilizes, worsens, connects to the old purpose or reveals a third path.
